title: MACH
summary: Brand strategy, identity and website for a portable virtual-production studio.
disciplines: Brand Strategy · Identity · Creative Direction · Digital

sections.heading: Virtual production could do incredible things.
body: But access to it was still expensive, complex, and built around large productions.
MACH set out to change that.
sections.statement: World-class production, without the usual constraints.

media.alt: A figure at the centre of a luminous, half-built desert world
A figure between LED panels of fire, the scene intentionally incomplete

sections.heading: MACH lives between two worlds.
body: The machine. Real-time technology, virtual environments, tracking, motion capture.
The imagination. Directors, artists, stories, ideas.
The brand needed to make both feel natural.
sections.statement: Creative enough to excite. Technical enough to trust.

media.alt: A film crew on the LED volume, a Nordic lake on the wall behind them

sections.heading: MACH wasn't built around a studio. It was built around the production.
body: Portable infrastructure means the studio can travel to the project, wherever it is.

media.alt: An ancient fig-tree forest, extreme wide
An architectural visualisation at dusk, mirrored in water
A bustling public waterfront at golden hour
A panoramic mountain valley with a lone figure

sections.heading: Fast, experimental and capable.
body: The visual language combines cinematic imagery, bold typography, motion and technology to create a brand that feels fast, experimental and capable.
The website extends that language into an experience that shows the work first and explains the technology second.
sections.statement: Don't tell people what MACH can do. Let them imagine what they could make.
